title: The caller record reads whose terminal it is from CAIRN_USER and CAIRN_OPERATOR
intention: caller() names whose hand a process is: a measured or declared Claude (cgroup ancestry, CAIRN_USER, or CLAUDECODE) is cc and is never upgraded to the operator; otherwise CAIRN_OPERATOR names the operator, so Akien's own terminal reads as Akien instead of unknown.
why: Akien 2026-10-13 (verbatim at ideas/2026-10-13-so-lets-talk-first-about-the-cairn.json): "we set CAIRN_OPERATOR= this can be OPERATOR or Akien or whatever... Akien is a subclass of operator, and mostly this gets used for reporting... but when we use cairn superclaude or cairn cc0 or cairn librarian or whatever... we also set the otherwise unset variable CAIRN_USER= which can be librarian or cc0 or whatever. if CAIRN_USER is set, then it's you... if it's not, then it's me." He set export CAIRN_OPERATOR=Akien in ~/.bashrc (line 166) the same day. Measured 2026-10-13: artifact.py caller() (:207) decides the class from cgroups alone (classify :164); a terminal Akien opens on the same box as CC's often classifies 'unknown', which is the questions-answer-unknown trouble (someone answered a question and the system could not tell who) and the 2026-10-12 idea for-the-record-you-can-t-recognize. Every Claude Code shell carries CLAUDECODE=1 (measured in this session), and Claude Code snapshots ~/.bashrc, so after a restart CC's shells carry CAIRN_OPERATOR=Akien too: the env rule must let CC evidence win.
traces_to: Law 6 (the owner alone gates writes, so the record of whose hand wrote must name a hand) and Law 7 (a record of truth says who, rather than 'unknown'); Akien's spec verbatim in why.
how: cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py only, in caller() after the ancestry decision: (a) if the class is cc: who = os.environ.get('CAIRN_USER') or 'cc'. (b) elif CAIRN_USER or CLAUDECODE is set (non-empty): class = 'cc', via = 'env', who = CAIRN_USER or 'cc'. (c) elif the class is akien: who = CAIRN_OPERATOR or 'akien'. (d) elif the class is unknown and CAIRN_OPERATOR is set: class = 'akien', via = 'env', who = CAIRN_OPERATOR. (e) gate is unchanged (who = 'gate'); unknown with nothing set stays unknown (who = None). The record gains keys 'who' and, when env decided, 'via': 'env'. The environment is read through one helper _env(name) so a proof can inject it; nothing else changes.
falsifier: cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_the_caller_reads_whose_terminal_it_is.py under PROVES {'8a53046951bb': {'1','2','3','4','5'}} with ancestry and the environment injected: (1) leaf unknown, CAIRN_OPERATOR=Akien, no CAIRN_USER, no CLAUDECODE -> class akien, who Akien, via env; (2) leaf unknown, CAIRN_USER=cc0, CAIRN_OPERATOR=Akien -> class cc, who cc0; (3) leaf unknown, CLAUDECODE=1, CAIRN_OPERATOR=Akien -> class cc, who cc; (4) a cc scope in the ancestry, CAIRN_OPERATOR=Akien, nothing else -> class cc (the env cannot upgrade a measured cc); (5) leaf unknown, nothing set -> class unknown, who None. Hollow: today's artifact.py reds 1, 2 and 3 (no who; unknown stays unknown).

decisions.text: Claude evidence always wins over CAIRN_OPERATOR: the env can resolve 'unknown' to the operator but can never turn a measured or declared Claude into Akien's hand, because Claude Code's shells inherit ~/.bashrc. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12
This is reporting-grade identity, as Akien said ('mostly this gets used for reporting'); authenticating his hand stays with its own open idea. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12

Add to cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py directly above 'def caller() -> dict:' exactly: 'def _env(name: str) -> str:' / '    """One environment variable, empty when unset: the one place caller() reads the environment (8a53046951bb)."""' / '    return os.environ.get(name) or ""'. os is already imported. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED'

In caller(), between the existing ancestry 'if me["class"] != "cc" and any(...)' block and the line 'me["ancestry"] = [...]', insert exactly: 'if me["class"] == "cc":' / '    me["who"] = _env("CAIRN_USER") or "cc"' / 'elif _env("CAIRN_USER") or _env("CLAUDECODE"):' / '    me.update({"class": "cc", "who": _env("CAIRN_USER") or "cc", "via": "env"})' / 'elif me["class"] == "akien":' / '    me["who"] = _env("CAIRN_OPERATOR") or "akien"' / 'elif me["class"] == "unknown" and _env("CAIRN_OPERATOR"):' / '    me.update({"class": "akien", "who": _env("CAIRN_OPERATOR"), "via": "env"})' / 'elif me["class"] == "gate":' / '    me["who"] = "gate"' / 'else:' / '    me["who"] = None', preceded by a three-line comment citing 8a53046951bb and Akien's 'if CAIRN_USER is set, then it's you... if it's not, then it's me.' The docstring gains one sentence: the environment then names whose hand it is, and can never turn a measured cc into akien. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED'
